chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn Nadr, from Amr ibn Nu'man Al-Ju'fi, who said:

There was a friend of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who rarely left his side. Whenever he went to a place, the friend would go with him. One time, while they were walking among the shoemakers, and with them was a Sindian slave boy walking behind them, the man turned around three times looking for his slave but did not see him. When he looked a fourth time, he said, 'O son of the adulteress! Where were you?'

He said: So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) raised his hand and struck his own forehead with it, then said, 'Glory be to Allah! You slander his mother. I used to think you had piety (war'), but it appears you do not.' The man said, 'May I be your ransom! His mother is a Sindian woman, a polytheist.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Do you not know that for every community there is a form of marriage? Stay away from me.'
He said: So I did not see him walking with him until death separated the two of them.
And in another report, he said: 'For every community there is a form of marriage by which they are restrained from adultery.'
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'for every community there is a marriage' in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Imam’s precision in linguistic usage (*lughah*) and social etiquette, correcting the companion’s assumption that a polytheist woman’s marital status was invalid merely due to her faith. The phrase 'for every community there is a marriage' (*li-kulli ummatin nikah*) highlights the Shia scholarly view that non-Muslims possess valid *nikah* within their own legal frameworks, thereby preserving their honor and preventing unjust accusations of adultery (*zina*). This incident underscores the importance of verifying facts before attributing moral failings to others, a key principle in Shia jurisprudence and character building.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Salim, from Ahmad Bin Nazar, from Amro Bin Nu’man Al Ju’fy who said,

‘There used to be a friend for Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> who was almost never separate from him<sup>asws</sup> whenever he<sup>asws</sup> went to a place. So while he was walking with him<sup>asws</sup> among the shoemakers, and with him was a Sindy slave of his walking behind him, when the man turned around intending his slave, three times, but did not see him. So when he looked during the fourth (time), he said, ‘O son of the adulteress! Where were you?’

He (the narrator) said, ‘So Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> raised his<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> hand and hit his<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> own forehead with it, then said: ‘Glory be to Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>! You slander his mother, and I<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> used to view the piety being for you, but there is no piety for you’. So he said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>! His mother was a Sindy woman, a Polytheist’. So he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘But don’t you know that for every community there is a (form of) marriage? Stay away from me<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>’.
He (the narrator) said: ‘So I did not see him<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> walking with him until the death separated the two of them’.
And in another report, ‘(He<sup>asws</sup> said): ‘For every community there is a (form of) marriage by which they are being withheld from the adultery’.
en.sarwar: 5. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from from Muhammad ibn Salim from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr from ‘ Amr ibn Nu’man al-Ju’fi who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) had a friend who almost all the time accompanied him whenever he went somewhere. Once he was walking with the Imam in the shoemaker’s place and his (man’s) slave from Sind was walking behind them. The man looked to find where his slave was. He could not see him. He tried three times and could not find him. At the fourth time he found him and said, ‘Where have you been, O son of a fornicating woman?’

The narrator has said that the Imam raised his hand and hit his own forehead and said, ‘All glory belongs to Allah, how you could accuse his mother? I considered you a pious person (restraining from sins). Now it shows you have no piety and restraint against evil.’ The man said, ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, his mother is a Sindy, (a pagan).’ The Imam said, ‘Did you not know that every people have a system of marriage? Stay away from me.’
The narrator has said that thereafter I never saw him walk with the Imam until death separated them from each other.
’ “In another Hadith it says, ‘Every people have a system of marriage. It keeps them reserved and away from fornication.’”
